preamble: Replacement of the postalveolar affricate [tʃ] by a plain alveolar stop [t] drops the fricative release and the postalveolar place. It arises where a speaker's system lacks [tʃ]: Māori, which has no affricates or sibilants, renders English /tʃ/ as t in loanwords such as tiamana 'chairman' and tīhi 'cheese'.

examples.note: English /tʃ/ is replaced by t, since Māori has no affricates; listed as a loanword in Te Aka Māori Dictionary.
Initial /tʃ/ becomes t, while /z/ becomes h.

sources: Smith, N. V. (1973). The Acquisition of Phonology: A Case Study. Cambridge University Press. https://talkbank.org/phon/access/Eng-UK/0docs/smith1973.pdf
